clues.text: This capital city sits on the high west end of Java in Indonesia. It lies a short trip southeast of Jakarta, the national capital.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside western Java in Indonesia

source.quote: Bandung is the capital city of the West Java province of Indonesia. Located on the western highland of Java island, it has one of the coolest climates compared to other provincial capitals in Indonesia, situated 708 meters (2,323 feet) above sea level (the highest point being at an altitude of 892 meters (2,927 feet) in the north, and the lowest at 666 meters (2,185 feet) in the south), approximately 145 kilometres (90 miles) southeast of Jakarta.

clues.text: High land gives this city cool air for this part of the world. It is one of the coolest capitals in all of Indonesia.
clues.narrowing: rules out the hot lowland capitals of Indonesia

clues.text: Dutch rulers gave it a town government in 1906. It soon grew into a fine resort town for Europeans.
clues.narrowing: rules out Indonesian cities without a 1906 Dutch town government

source.quote: In the early 20th century, the Dutch population in Bandung demanded the establishment of a municipal government (gemeente) a request granted in 1906 and the city subsequently developed into an exclusive resort area for Europeans, complete with hotels, cafés, and shops.

clues.text: Dutch rulers planned to move the colonial capital to this city. Its ring of volcanic peaks formed a natural shield.
clues.narrowing: rules out capitals the Dutch never planned to move their seat to

source.quote: Bandung lies in a river basin surrounded by volcanic mountains that provide a natural defense system, which was the primary reason for the Dutch East Indies government's plan to move the capital from Batavia (modern-day Jakarta) to Bandung.

clues.text: Dutch planters set up tea farms in the hills here long ago. They planted tea all around the mountain slopes.
